The unit "pm/(m-C)" is a rendering corruption of "um/(m-C)": the reference Stratasys ULTEM 9085 FDM datasheet reports mean CTE per ASTM E831 between 31.35 and 51.88 um/[m*C] for the same resin, and pm/(m-C) is ~6 orders of magnitude from any polymer CTE. Unit reading is therefore supported, but NOT applied: the 629.9 cross-flow ZX figure remains more than 10x any published PEI value and cannot be reconciled, so no CTE is normalized from this table. PEI is outside the H2C envelope, so this is low priority. Action: request the original ASTM E831 report.

Resolved as non-blocking 2026-09-11. The H2C hardware baseline is 350 C nozzle / 120 C bed / 65 C chamber (Method H2C row; confirmed on the Bambu H2C specification page). Every published 3DXTECH PEEK range exceeds it - the current TDS printed-specimen block gives 380-400 C nozzle and 130-140 C bed, and both previously recorded ranges (360-450/120-160 and 400-480/140-180) are also out of envelope. The conflict therefore cannot change the exclusion, and both ranges are retained without reconciliation.

Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data.
